{"text":"ItemID: unavailable; Title: Kill Box 13; ALIGN: yes; RATING: NA; REASON: Its thrash sound fits my heavier listening, but I would choose melodic metal first today.
ItemID: unavailable; Title: Comalies; ALIGN: yes; RATING: 4; REASON: The melodic vocals and heavy guitars appeal to the side of my taste drawn to In Flames and Soilwork.
ItemID: unavailable; Title: Every Man For Himself; ALIGN: yes; RATING: NA; REASON: Hoobastank fits my interest in The Reason, but I am more interested in heavier music this visit.
ItemID: unavailable; Title: Shot to Hell; ALIGN: yes; RATING: NA; REASON: The heavy riffs sound appealing, though I would prioritize the melodic metal choices here.
ItemID: unavailable; Title: Lullabies to Paralyze       explicit_lyrics; ALIGN: yes; RATING: NA; REASON: The darker hard rock could suit my mood, but it is a less direct match than Stabbing the Drama.
ItemID: unavailable; Title: Night at the Opera; ALIGN: no; RATING: NA; REASON: The title alone leaves me unsure which album this is, so I would pass this time.
ItemID: unavailable; Title: October Rust; ALIGN: yes; RATING: NA; REASON: Its dark, melodic heaviness interests me, but I want something more driving right now.
ItemID: unavailable; Title: Peeping Tom; ALIGN: no; RATING: NA; REASON: The experimental crossover sound is less aligned with the guitar-driven metal I want today.
ItemID: unavailable; Title: Scum; ALIGN: no; RATING: NA; REASON: The abrasive grindcore approach is less appealing right now than metal with stronger melodic hooks.
ItemID: unavailable; Title: Stabbing the Drama; ALIGN: yes; RATING: 5; REASON: I already listen to Figure Number Five, so another Soilwork album with melodic hooks and aggressive riffs is my strongest choice."}
